questions.q: According to the factor theorem, if P(x) is a polynomial and P(3) = 0, which statement is true?

questions.why: The factor theorem states that if substituting x = c gives P(c) = 0, then the linear expression (x − c) divides P(x) exactly without remainder.

questions.q: When p(x) = x³ + ax − 6 is divided by (x − 2), the remainder is 4. Find a.
questions.why: By the remainder theorem p(2) = 4, so 8 + 2a − 6 = 4, giving 2a = 2 and a = 1. Using p(−2) instead gives −9.

questions.q: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 5 and xy = 6.
questions.why: Substitute y = 5 − x: x(5 − x) = 6, so x² − 5x + 6 = 0 and (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. Each x gives y from y = 5 − x.

questions.q: The line y = 2x + c is a tangent to the curve y = x² + 3. Find c.
questions.why: x² + 3 = 2x + c gives x² − 2x + (3 − c) = 0. A tangent meets the curve once, so b² − 4ac = 4 − 4(3 − c) = 0, giving c = 2.

questions.q: Which is the equation of the circle with centre (3, −2) that passes through the point (6, 2)?
questions.why: r² = (6 − 3)² + (2 + 2)² = 9 + 16 = 25, and centre (3, −2) gives (x − 3)² + (y + 2)². The right-hand side is r², not r.

questions.q: Find the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² + 4x − 10y + 20 = 0.
questions.why: Complete the square: (x + 2)² − 4 + (y − 5)² − 25 + 20 = 0, so (x + 2)² + (y − 5)² = 9. The centre is (−2, 5) and the radius is √9 = 3.

questions.q: In how many ways can 4 books be chosen from a shelf of 9 distinct books if the order of selection does not matter?
questions.why: Combinations are used when order does not matter: 9C4 = 9! / (4! 5!) = (9 × 8 × 7 × 6) / (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 126.

questions.why: The first letter can be E or I (2 ways), then the other 5 letters can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways, giving 2 × 120 = 240.
